I treat every 1-2 weeks. Whatever does come back I have treated again and there is less to treat each time.  It's more tedious than IPL for sure, but the success rate per treated hair seems good. reviews.t: You need to have excellent hand eye coordination and have the ability to hold ...
reviews.x: This product actually works. You need to have excellent hand eye coordination and have the ability to hold the wand steady. I found it difficult to do when the buzzing sound began. It took 2-3 uses per hair for me, and the skin reaction took about a week to heal. However, when the entire hair shaft came out with the tweezers I knew I had found a solution to what had been an absolute nightmare for me.

reviews.t: It really does work.
reviews.x: It really works. I was skeptical because of the reviews I read, but if you follow the directions exactly as written, it really works. I have PCOS so my facial hair grows in like a man's does, it's coarse and think and this works! The only problem I have is that I tend to jump a little when it's working and sometimes pull the wire out of my pore but that's just a natural reflex when electrocuting oneself.

The instructions are a bit lacking but an understanding of what you are trying to accomplish helps. reviews.t: Good idea but doesn’t work well.
reviews.x: I tried to do electrolysis on my chin. I’m pretty handy with DIY cosmetic procedures. Well, this didn’t work out very well. It’s very hard to do this on yourself because you have to insert the probe into the hair follicle. I tried, and “buzzed” the hair several times. Nothing happened. Next day I had a small raised welt on my chin. 2 days later the welt is still there. I do not recommend this machine to do electrolysis on your own face. I will have to go back to my professional electrologist.

reviews.t: Blessed when good things endure the passage of time... this is one!
reviews.x: I bought a similar unit [[ASIN:B00011JN5G Clean + Easy Deluxe Electrolysis Home (For Coarse Hair)]] back in 1969 and had such great success with my brows and legs and with my husbands beard that we have never had to shave since!  Well... now my old hormones are dying and my facial hairs are starting to become obvious, but not for long! Praise God that this little gem is still around and folks can still afford it. Nearly 50 years of freedom and looking forward to more!

Was too painful so I decided to just return it.

claims.text: Most reviewers agree the device actually works for permanent hair removal, often compared favorably to professional electrolysis.
Many reviewers warn the process is slow, tedious, and requires patience and practice to get results.
Several reviewers note it can be painful or cause burns/skin reactions, especially at higher settings.
A few reviewers report poor build quality or breakage, with one calling it a waste of money.
Some reviewers find it useful for touch-ups or targeting finer facial hairs like mustache and chin.
